+# The Daily Grind
+
+Static homepage with private, browser-local delivery notes. Install with `pnpm install`; regenerate the committed browser bundle with `pnpm build`. Cryptographic checks: `node --test tests/crypto.test.js`.
+
+## Encryption and storage
+
+Each save encapsulates a fresh shared secret to a persistent recipient public key using `@noble/post-quantum`'s ML-KEM-768 + X25519 hybrid (X-Wing). The bundled implementation preserves hybrid protection without depending on experimental native KEM APIs or a runtime CDN. WebCrypto HKDF-SHA256 derives a non-extractable AES-256-GCM message key with a random salt and protocol metadata as context. Each message has a fresh 96-bit IV and 128-bit authentication tag. Version, suite, recipient ID, record ID and timestamp are authenticated as additional data.
+
+IndexedDB stores the ciphertext envelope and recipient key material. The recipient secret is wrapped using AES-GCM under a non-extractable WebCrypto key, also persisted in IndexedDB. Raw secret bytes are transient and cleared on completion where possible; JavaScript cannot guarantee erasure of all runtime copies. Plaintext notes are never sent to a server, placed in URLs, logged, or saved. Revealed notes use textContent and are hidden when the tab becomes hidden. Export contains only the encrypted envelope; it does not contain recipient keys and is not independently recoverable.
+
+This is a **local feature**, not an end-to-end delivery service: there is no order API or driver key infrastructure in this repository. For delivery integration, provision and authenticate the actual delivery recipient's public key, use a separate private-key trust boundary, and submit only envelopes with authenticated order identifiers. Never ship a recipient private key in the public bundle. Same-origin script compromise, malicious browser extensions, or access to an unlocked browser can still read notes or invoke local keys. Browser data deletion loses both notes and keys. HTTPS (or a trustworthy localhost origin) and IndexedDB are required. Encryption failures do not fall back to plaintext.

+import { createRecipient, encryptNote, decryptNote } from './crypto.js';
+
+const form = document.querySelector('#notes-form');
+const controls = document.querySelector('#note-controls');
+const input = document.querySelector('#delivery-note');
+const count = document.querySelector('#character-count');
+const status = document.querySelector('#note-status');
+const saved = document.querySelector('#saved-note');
+const revealed = document.querySelector('#decrypted-note');
+const revealButton = document.querySelector('#reveal-note');
+const saveButton = document.querySelector('#save-note');
+let database, recipient, envelope;
+
+function announce(message, error = false) {
+  status.textContent = message;
+  status.classList.toggle('error', error);
+}
+function updateCount() { count.textContent = `${input.value.length} / 500`; }
+function hidePlaintext() {
+  revealed.textContent = '';
+  revealed.hidden = true;
+  revealButton.textContent = 'Reveal note';
+  revealButton.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
+}
+function request(operation, mode = 'readonly') {
+  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
+    const transaction = database.transaction('vault', mode);
+    const result = operation(transaction.objectStore('vault'));
+    transaction.oncomplete = () => resolve(result?.result);
+    transaction.onerror = () => reject(transaction.error);
+    transaction.onabort = () => reject(transaction.error || new Error('Storage transaction aborted.'));
+  });
+}
+async function initialize() {
+  try {
+    if (!globalThis.isSecureContext || !crypto.subtle || !globalThis.indexedDB) throw new Error('Secure storage unavailable');
+    database = await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
+      const opening = indexedDB.open('daily-grind-private-notes', 1);
+      opening.onupgradeneeded = () => opening.result.createObjectStore('vault');
+      opening.onsuccess = () => resolve(opening.result);
+      opening.onerror = () => reject(opening.error);
+      opening.onblocked = () => reject(new Error('Storage blocked'));
+    });
+    // A single atomic add selects the same recipient key even if two tabs initialize together.
+    recipient = await request((store) => store.get('recipient'));
+    if (!recipient) {
+      const generated = await createRecipient();
+      try { await request((store) => store.add(generated, 'recipient'), 'readwrite'); }
+      catch { /* Another tab may have installed the key first. Read the committed value below. */ }
+      recipient = await request((store) => store.get('recipient'));
+      if (!recipient) throw new Error('Unable to persist recipient key');
+    }
+    envelope = await request((store) => store.get('note'));
+    saved.hidden = !envelope;
+    controls.disabled = false;
+    announce(envelope ? 'Your encrypted note is saved on this device.' : '');
+    database.onversionchange = () => { database.close(); controls.disabled = true; announce('Storage changed. Reload this page to continue.', true); };
+  } catch {
+    announce('Secure storage is unavailable. Use HTTPS and allow browser storage, then reload. Your note has not been saved.', true);
+  }
+}
+// Always prevent submission, including while crypto initialization fails.
+form.addEventListener('submit', async (event) => {
+  event.preventDefault();
+  input.setCustomValidity(input.value.trim() ? '' : 'Please enter delivery instructions.');
+  if (!form.reportValidity() || !recipient) return;
+  saveButton.disabled = true;
+  saveButton.textContent = 'Encrypting…';
+  try {
+    const next = await encryptNote(recipient, input.value);
+    await request((store) => store.put(next, 'note'), 'readwrite');
+    envelope = next;
+    hidePlaintext();
+    input.value = '';
+    updateCount();
+    saved.hidden = false;
+    announce('Encrypted and saved on this device. No note was sent with an order.');
+  } catch {
+    announce('Your note could not be saved. Please try again; your draft is still here.', true);
+  } finally {
+    saveButton.disabled = false;
+    saveButton.textContent = 'Encrypt & save note';
+  }
+});
+input.addEventListener('input', () => { input.setCustomValidity(''); updateCount(); });
+document.querySelectorAll('[data-note]').forEach((button) => button.addEventListener('click', () => {
+  const note = button.dataset.note;
+  const next = input.value.trim() ? `${input.value.trim()} ${note}` : note;
+  if (next.length > 500) { announce('There is not enough room for that instruction. Shorten your note first.', true); return; }
+  input.value = next;
+  input.setCustomValidity('');
+  updateCount();
+  input.focus();
+}));

+import { ml_kem768_x25519 as hybrid } from '@noble/post-quantum/hybrid.js';
+
+const encode = new TextEncoder();
+const suite = 'MLKEM768-X25519+HKDF-SHA256+AES-256-GCM';
+const random = (size) => crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(size));
+export const toBase64 = (bytes) => btoa(String.fromCharCode(...new Uint8Array(bytes)));
+const fromBase64 = (value) => Uint8Array.from(atob(value), (char) => char.charCodeAt(0));
+const context = (header) => encode.encode(JSON.stringify(header));
+
+// Only the public key, wrapped secret, and non-extractable wrapping CryptoKey persist.
+export async function createRecipient() {
+  const { publicKey, secretKey } = hybrid.keygen();
+  const storageKey = await crypto.subtle.generateKey({ name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256 }, false, ['encrypt', 'decrypt']);
+  const id = crypto.randomUUID();
+  const iv = random(12);
+  try {
+    const wrappedSecret = await crypto.subtle.encrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv, additionalData: encode.encode(id) }, storageKey, secretKey);
+    return { id, publicKey, storageKey, iv, wrappedSecret };
+  } finally {
+    secretKey.fill(0);
+  }
+}
+
+async function deriveKey(secret, salt, header) {
+  const material = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', secret, 'HKDF', false, ['deriveKey']);
+  return crypto.subtle.deriveKey({ name: 'HKDF', hash: 'SHA-256', salt, info: context(header) }, material, { name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256 }, false, ['encrypt', 'decrypt']);
+}
+
+export async function encryptNote(recipient, note) {
+  if (typeof note !== 'string' || !note.trim() || note.length > 500) throw new Error('Enter a note of 1–500 characters.');
+  const { cipherText, sharedSecret } = hybrid.encapsulate(recipient.publicKey);
+  const header = { version: 1, suite, recipient: recipient.id, id: crypto.randomUUID(), createdAt: new Date().toISOString() };
+  const salt = random(32);
+  const iv = random(12);
+  const plaintext = encode.encode(note);
+  try {
+    const key = await deriveKey(sharedSecret, salt, header);
+    const ciphertext = await crypto.subtle.encrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv, additionalData: context(header), tagLength: 128 }, key, plaintext);
+    return { header, capsule: toBase64(cipherText), salt: toBase64(salt), iv: toBase64(iv), ciphertext: toBase64(ciphertext) };
+  } finally {
+    sharedSecret.fill(0);
+    plaintext.fill(0);
+  }
+}
+
+export async function decryptNote(recipient, envelope) {
+  if (envelope.header.version !== 1 || envelope.header.suite !== suite || envelope.header.recipient !== recipient.id) throw new Error('This note does not match the recipient key.');
+  let privateBytes, sharedSecret, plaintext;
+  try {
+    privateBytes = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.decrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv: recipient.iv, additionalData: encode.encode(recipient.id) }, recipient.storageKey, recipient.wrappedSecret));
+    sharedSecret = hybrid.decapsulate(fromBase64(envelope.capsule), privateBytes);
+    const key = await deriveKey(sharedSecret, fromBase64(envelope.salt), envelope.header);
+    plaintext = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.decrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv: fromBase64(envelope.iv), additionalData: context(envelope.header), tagLength: 128 }, key, fromBase64(envelope.ciphertext)));
+    return new TextDecoder().decode(plaintext);
+  } finally {
+    privateBytes?.fill(0);
+    sharedSecret?.fill(0);
+    plaintext?.fill(0);
+  }
+}

+import test from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { createRecipient, encryptNote, decryptNote } from '../src/crypto.js';
+
+test('hybrid notes round-trip after structured cloning and never serialize plaintext', async () => {
+  const recipient = structuredClone(await createRecipient());
+  const note = 'Gate 0482. Please knock softly. ☕';
+  const envelope = await encryptNote(recipient, note);
+  assert.equal(await decryptNote(recipient, JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(envelope))), note);
+  assert.equal(JSON.stringify(envelope).includes(note), false);
+  assert.equal(recipient.storageKey.extractable, false);
+  await assert.rejects(crypto.subtle.exportKey('raw', recipient.storageKey));
+  const second = await encryptNote(recipient, note);
+  assert.notEqual(envelope.iv, second.iv);
+  assert.notEqual(envelope.capsule, second.capsule);
+  assert.notEqual(envelope.ciphertext, second.ciphertext);
+});
+
+test('rejects altered ciphertext, capsule, nonce, salt, metadata and wrong recipients', async () => {
+  const recipient = await createRecipient();
+  const envelope = await encryptNote(recipient, 'Private instructions');
+  for (const field of ['ciphertext', 'capsule', 'iv', 'salt']) {
+    const changed = structuredClone(envelope);
+    const bytes = Buffer.from(changed[field], 'base64');
+    bytes[0] ^= 1;
+    changed[field] = bytes.toString('base64');
+    await assert.rejects(decryptNote(recipient, changed), `${field} tampering must fail`);
+  }
+  for (const field of ['id', 'createdAt', 'suite', 'version', 'recipient']) {
+    const changed = structuredClone(envelope);
+    changed.header[field] = 'tampered';
+    await assert.rejects(decryptNote(recipient, changed), `${field} tampering must fail`);
+  }
+  await assert.rejects(decryptNote(await createRecipient(), envelope));
+});
+
+test('rejects empty and oversized notes', async () => {
+  const recipient = await createRecipient();
+  for (const note of ['', '   ', 'a'.repeat(501)]) await assert.rejects(encryptNote(recipient, note));
+});

+/* All path tracing executes in the compiled C++ WebAssembly module. */
+importScripts('./smallpt.js');
+self.onmessage = async ({ data }) => {
+  try {
+    const module = await createSmallpt({ locateFile: (name) => new URL(name, self.location.href).href });
+    const { width, height, samples, seed, colors } = data;
+    module._setup(width, height, seed, ...colors.flat());
+    const started = performance.now();
+    const passes = samples / 4;
+    let lastUpdate = 0;
+    for (let pass = 0; pass < passes; pass++) {
+      for (let row = 0; row < height; row += 8) {
+        module._render_rows(row, Math.min(8, height - row));
+        const now = performance.now();
+        if (now - lastUpdate > 150) {
+          self.postMessage({ type: 'progress', progress: (pass + Math.min(row+8,height)/height) / passes, elapsed: now-started, samples: pass*4 });
+          lastUpdate = now;
+        }
+      }
+      module._finish_pass();
+      const pixels = module.HEAPU8.slice(module._framebuffer(), module._framebuffer() + width*height*4);
+      self.postMessage({ type: 'frame', pixels, samples: (pass+1)*4, progress: (pass+1)/passes, elapsed: performance.now()-started }, [pixels.buffer]);
+    }
+    self.postMessage({ type: 'done', elapsed: performance.now()-started });
+  } catch (error) {
+    self.postMessage({ type: 'error', message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) });
+  }
+};

+#include <math.h>   // smallpt, a Path Tracer by Kevin Beason, 2008
+#include <stdlib.h> // Make : g++ -O3 -fopenmp smallpt.cpp -o smallpt
+#include <stdio.h>  //        Remove "-fopenmp" for g++ version < 4.2
+struct Vec {        // Usage: time ./smallpt 5000 && xv image.ppm
+  double x, y, z;                  // position, also color (r,g,b)
+  Vec(double x_=0, double y_=0, double z_=0){ x=x_; y=y_; z=z_; }
+  Vec operator+(const Vec &b) const { return Vec(x+b.x,y+b.y,z+b.z); }
+  Vec operator-(const Vec &b) const { return Vec(x-b.x,y-b.y,z-b.z); }
+  Vec operator*(double b) const { return Vec(x*b,y*b,z*b); }
+  Vec mult(const Vec &b) const { return Vec(x*b.x,y*b.y,z*b.z); }
+  Vec& norm(){ return *this = *this * (1/sqrt(x*x+y*y+z*z)); }
+  double dot(const Vec &b) const { return x*b.x+y*b.y+z*b.z; } // cross:
+  Vec operator%(Vec&b){return Vec(y*b.z-z*b.y,z*b.x-x*b.z,x*b.y-y*b.x);}
+};
+struct Ray { Vec o, d; Ray(Vec o_, Vec d_) : o(o_), d(d_) {} };
+enum Refl_t { DIFF, SPEC, REFR };  // material types, used in radiance()
+struct Sphere {
+  double rad;       // radius
+  Vec p, e, c;      // position, emission, color
+  Refl_t refl;      // reflection type (DIFFuse, SPECular, REFRactive)
+  Sphere(double rad_, Vec p_, Vec e_, Vec c_, Refl_t refl_):
+    rad(rad_), p(p_), e(e_), c(c_), refl(refl_) {}
+  double intersect(const Ray &r) const { // returns distance, 0 if nohit
+    Vec op = p-r.o; // Solve t^2*d.d + 2*t*(o-p).d + (o-p).(o-p)-R^2 = 0
+    double t, eps=1e-4, b=op.dot(r.d), det=b*b-op.dot(op)+rad*rad;
+    if (det<0) return 0; else det=sqrt(det);
+    return (t=b-det)>eps ? t : ((t=b+det)>eps ? t : 0);
+  }
+};
+Sphere spheres[] = {//Scene: radius, position, emission, color, material
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec( 1e5+1,40.8,81.6), Vec(),Vec(.75,.25,.25),DIFF),//Left
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(-1e5+99,40.8,81.6),Vec(),Vec(.25,.25,.75),DIFF),//Rght
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50,40.8, 1e5),     Vec(),Vec(.75,.75,.75),DIFF),//Back
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50,40.8,-1e5+170), Vec(),Vec(),           DIFF),//Frnt
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50, 1e5, 81.6),    Vec(),Vec(.75,.75,.75),DIFF),//Botm
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50,-1e5+81.6,81.6),Vec(),Vec(.75,.75,.75),DIFF),//Top
+  Sphere(16.5,Vec(27,16.5,47),       Vec(),Vec(1,1,1)*.999, SPEC),//Mirr
+  Sphere(16.5,Vec(73,16.5,78),       Vec(),Vec(1,1,1)*.999, REFR),//Glas
+  Sphere(600, Vec(50,681.6-.27,81.6),Vec(12,12,12),  Vec(), DIFF) //Lite
+};
+inline double clamp(double x){ return x<0 ? 0 : x>1 ? 1 : x; }
+inline int toInt(double x){ return int(pow(clamp(x),1/2.2)*255+.5); }
+inline bool intersect(const Ray &r, double &t, int &id){
+  double n=sizeof(spheres)/sizeof(Sphere), d, inf=t=1e20;
+  for(int i=int(n);i--;) if((d=spheres[i].intersect(r))&&d<t){t=d;id=i;}
+  return t<inf;
+}
+Vec radiance(const Ray &r, int depth, unsigned short *Xi){
+  double t;                               // distance to intersection
+  int id=0;                               // id of intersected object
+  if (!intersect(r, t, id)) return Vec(); // if miss, return black
+  const Sphere &obj = spheres[id];        // the hit object
+  Vec x=r.o+r.d*t, n=(x-obj.p).norm(), nl=n.dot(r.d)<0?n:n*-1, f=obj.c;
+  double p = f.x>f.y && f.x>f.z ? f.x : f.y>f.z ? f.y : f.z; // max refl
+  if (++depth>5) if (erand48(Xi)<p) f=f*(1/p); else return obj.e; //R.R.
+  if (obj.refl == DIFF){                  // Ideal DIFFUSE reflection
+    double r1=2*M_PI*erand48(Xi), r2=erand48(Xi), r2s=sqrt(r2);
+    Vec w=nl, u=((fabs(w.x)>.1?Vec(0,1):Vec(1))%w).norm(), v=w%u;
+    Vec d = (u*cos(r1)*r2s + v*sin(r1)*r2s + w*sqrt(1-r2)).norm();
+    return obj.e + f.mult(radiance(Ray(x,d),depth,Xi));
+  } else if (obj.refl == SPEC)            // Ideal SPECULAR reflection
+    return obj.e + f.mult(radiance(Ray(x,r.d-n*2*n.dot(r.d)),depth,Xi));
+  Ray reflRay(x, r.d-n*2*n.dot(r.d));     // Ideal dielectric REFRACTION
+  bool into = n.dot(nl)>0;                // Ray from outside going in?
+  double nc=1, nt=1.5, nnt=into?nc/nt:nt/nc, ddn=r.d.dot(nl), cos2t;
+  if ((cos2t=1-nnt*nnt*(1-ddn*ddn))<0)    // Total internal reflection
+    return obj.e + f.mult(radiance(reflRay,depth,Xi));
+  Vec tdir = (r.d*nnt - n*((into?1:-1)*(ddn*nnt+sqrt(cos2t)))).norm();
+  double a=nt-nc, b=nt+nc, R0=a*a/(b*b), c = 1-(into?-ddn:tdir.dot(n));
+  double Re=R0+(1-R0)*c*c*c*c*c,Tr=1-Re,P=.25+.5*Re,RP=Re/P,TP=Tr/(1-P);
+  return obj.e + f.mult(depth>2 ? (erand48(Xi)<P ?   // Russian roulette
+    radiance(reflRay,depth,Xi)*RP:radiance(Ray(x,tdir),depth,Xi)*TP) :
+    radiance(reflRay,depth,Xi)*Re+radiance(Ray(x,tdir),depth,Xi)*Tr);
+}
+int main(int argc, char *argv[]){
+  int w=1024, h=768, samps = argc==2 ? atoi(argv[1])/4 : 1; // # samples
+  Ray cam(Vec(50,52,295.6), Vec(0,-0.042612,-1).norm()); // cam pos, dir
+  Vec cx=Vec(w*.5135/h), cy=(cx%cam.d).norm()*.5135, r, *c=new Vec[w*h];
+#pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic, 1) private(r)       // OpenMP
+  for (int y=0; y<h; y++){                       // Loop over image rows
+    fprintf(stderr,"\rRendering (%d spp) %5.2f%%",samps*4,100.*y/(h-1));
+    for (unsigned short x=0, Xi[3]={0,0,y*y*y}; x<w; x++)   // Loop cols
+      for (int sy=0, i=(h-y-1)*w+x; sy<2; sy++)     // 2x2 subpixel rows
+        for (int sx=0; sx<2; sx++, r=Vec()){        // 2x2 subpixel cols
+          for (int s=0; s<samps; s++){
+            double r1=2*erand48(Xi), dx=r1<1 ? sqrt(r1)-1: 1-sqrt(2-r1);
+            double r2=2*erand48(Xi), dy=r2<1 ? sqrt(r2)-1: 1-sqrt(2-r2);
+            Vec d = cx*( ( (sx+.5 + dx)/2 + x)/w - .5) +
+                    cy*( ( (sy+.5 + dy)/2 + y)/h - .5) + cam.d;
+            r = r + radiance(Ray(cam.o+d*140,d.norm()),0,Xi)*(1./samps);
+          } // Camera rays are pushed ^^^^^ forward to start in interior
+          c[i] = c[i] + Vec(clamp(r.x),clamp(r.y),clamp(r.z))*.25;
+        }
+  }
+  FILE *f = fopen("image.ppm", "w");         // Write image to PPM file.
+  fprintf(f, "P3\n%d %d\n%d\n", w, h, 255);
+  for (int i=0; i<w*h; i++)
+    fprintf(f,"%d %d %d ", toInt(c[i].x), toInt(c[i].y), toInt(c[i].z));
+}

+// Browser adapter for Kevin Beason's smallpt (MIT license, see LICENSE.txt).
+// The original path-tracing algorithm is included unchanged.
+#define main smallpt_original_main
+#include "smallpt-original.cpp"
+#undef main
+#include <stdint.h>
+#include <vector>
+#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__
+#include <emscripten/emscripten.h>
+#define EXPORT EMSCRIPTEN_KEEPALIVE
+#else
+#define EXPORT
+#endif
+
+static int width, height, passes;
+static uint32_t seed;
+static std::vector<Vec> accumulation;
+static std::vector<unsigned char> pixels;
+
+extern "C" {
+EXPORT void setup(int w, int h, uint32_t randomSeed,
+                  double ar, double ag, double ab,
+                  double br, double bg, double bb) {
+  width=w; height=h; seed=randomSeed; passes=0;
+  accumulation.assign(w*h, Vec());
+  pixels.assign(w*h*4, 0);
+  spheres[6].c=Vec(ar,ag,ab);
+  spheres[7].c=Vec(br,bg,bb);
+}
+// One pass adds four samples per pixel, using smallpt's 2x2 subpixel grid.
+EXPORT void render_rows(int start, int count) {
+  Ray cam(Vec(50,52,295.6), Vec(0,-0.042612,-1).norm());
+  Vec cx=Vec(width*.5135/height), cy=(cx%cam.d).norm()*.5135;
+  for(int y=start; y<start+count && y<height; ++y) {
+    uint32_t hash=seed ^ (uint32_t(y+1)*2654435761u) ^ (uint32_t(passes+1)*2246822519u);
+    unsigned short Xi[3]={(unsigned short)hash,(unsigned short)(hash>>16),(unsigned short)(y*y*y+passes+1)};
+    for(int x=0; x<width; ++x) {
+      Vec color;
+      for(int sy=0; sy<2; ++sy) for(int sx=0; sx<2; ++sx) {
+        double r1=2*erand48(Xi), dx=r1<1?sqrt(r1)-1:1-sqrt(2-r1);
+        double r2=2*erand48(Xi), dy=r2<1?sqrt(r2)-1:1-sqrt(2-r2);
+        Vec d=cx*(((sx+.5+dx)/2+x)/width-.5)+cy*(((sy+.5+dy)/2+y)/height-.5)+cam.d;
+        color=color+radiance(Ray(cam.o+d*140,d.norm()),0,Xi)*.25;
+      }
+      int i=(height-y-1)*width+x;
+      accumulation[i]=accumulation[i]+color;
+      Vec c=accumulation[i]*(1./(passes+1));
+      pixels[i*4]=toInt(c.x); pixels[i*4+1]=toInt(c.y); pixels[i*4+2]=toInt(c.z); pixels[i*4+3]=255;
+    }
+  }
+}
+EXPORT void finish_pass() { ++passes; }
+EXPORT unsigned char* framebuffer() { return pixels.data(); }
+}
+
+#ifdef SMALLPT_PREVIEW
+int main() {
+  setup(640,480,42,.999,.999,.999,.999,.999,.999);
+  for(int p=0;p<64;++p) { render_rows(0,480); finish_pass(); }
+  FILE* f=fopen("/tmp/smallpt-preview.rgba","wb");
+  fwrite(pixels.data(),1,pixels.size(),f); fclose(f);
+}
+#endif

+import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
+import vm from 'node:vm';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+const source = readFileSync(new URL('../public/wasm/smallpt.js',import.meta.url),'utf8');
+const binary = readFileSync(new URL('../public/wasm/smallpt.wasm',import.meta.url));
+const sandbox = { __dirname: new URL('../public/wasm/',import.meta.url).pathname, console, process, require:createRequire(import.meta.url), WebAssembly, Uint8Array, Int8Array, Uint32Array, ArrayBuffer, setTimeout };
+const context = vm.createContext(sandbox);

+  renderer._setup(64,48,42,...colors);
+  for(let i=0;i<4;i++) { renderer._render_rows(0,48); renderer._finish_pass(); }
+  return renderer.HEAPU8.slice(renderer._framebuffer(),renderer._framebuffer()+64*48*4);
+}
+const neutral = render([.999,.999,.999,.999,.999,.999]);
+const tinted = render([.95,.5,.6,.5,.9,.6]);
+assert.equal(neutral.length,64*48*4);
+assert.ok(neutral.some((n,i)=>i%4!==3&&n>0),'render contains lit pixels');
+assert.ok(neutral.every((n,i)=>i%4!==3||n===255),'all pixels are opaque');
+assert.notDeepEqual(neutral,tinted,'changing sphere colors changes the rendered image');
+assert.deepEqual(neutral,render([.999,.999,.999,.999,.999,.999]),'setup resets accumulation');

+  location: {href:'file:///wasm/render-worker.js'},

+const get = <T extends HTMLElement>(id: string) => document.getElementById(id) as T;
+const canvas = get<HTMLCanvasElement>('render');
+const context = canvas.getContext('2d')!;
+const quality = get<HTMLSelectElement>('quality');
+const resolution = get<HTMLSelectElement>('resolution');
+const preview = get<HTMLImageElement>('preview');
+const base = document.body.dataset.base || '/';
+let worker: Worker | undefined;
+let colors = [[.999,.999,.999],[.999,.999,.999]];
+let currentSamples = 64;
+let ready = false;
+let startedAt = 0;
+let downloading = false;
+
+function updateColors() {
+  const css = (color: number[]) => `rgb(${color.map(v => Math.round(v*255)).join(',')})`;
+  get('mirror-swatch').style.background = `linear-gradient(135deg, #fff, ${css(colors[0])} 55%, #82917d)`;
+  get('glass-swatch').style.background = `radial-gradient(circle at 30% 25%, #fff, ${css(colors[1])} 65%, #798d77)`;
+}
+function progress(value: number, elapsed: number, samples: number) {
+  get('progress').style.width = `${value*100}%`;
+  get('elapsed').textContent = `${(elapsed/1000).toFixed(1)}s`;
+  get('sample-count').textContent = `${samples} / ${currentSamples} spp`;
+}
+function render() {
+  worker?.terminate();
+  currentSamples = Number(quality.value);
+  const width = Number(resolution.value), height = width * .75;
+  startedAt = performance.now();
+  ready = false;
+  get('status').textContent = 'Rendering light paths…';
+  get('status-dot').classList.add('busy');
+  progress(0,0,0);
+  get('stage-resolution').textContent = `${width} × ${height}`;
+  try {
+    worker = new Worker(`${base}wasm/render-worker.js`);
+    worker.onmessage = ({data}) => {
+      if (data.type === 'frame') {
+        if (canvas.width !== width || canvas.height !== height) {
+          canvas.width = width; canvas.height = height;
+        }
+        context.putImageData(new ImageData(new Uint8ClampedArray(data.pixels), width, height),0,0);
+        preview.hidden = true;
+        preview.style.display = 'none';
+        ready = true;
+      }
+      if (data.type === 'frame' || data.type === 'progress') progress(data.progress, data.elapsed, data.samples);
+      if (data.type === 'done') {
+        progress(1, data.elapsed, currentSamples);
+        get('status').textContent = 'Render complete';
+        get('status-dot').classList.remove('busy');
+        worker?.terminate(); worker = undefined;
+      }
+      if (data.type === 'error') fail(data.message);
+    };
+    worker.onerror = (event) => fail(event.message || 'Unable to load renderer');
+    worker.postMessage({ width, height, samples: currentSamples, seed: crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint32Array(1))[0], colors });
+  } catch (error) { fail(String(error)); }
+}
+function fail(message: string) {
+  worker?.terminate(); worker = undefined;
+  get('status').textContent = 'Render unavailable · click Render again to retry';
+  get('status-dot').classList.remove('busy');
+  get('elapsed').textContent = `${((performance.now()-startedAt)/1000).toFixed(1)}s`;
+  console.error('smallpt:', message);
+}
+get('randomize').addEventListener('click', () => {
+  // Keep tinted reflective materials bright enough for light to travel through the scene.
+  colors = Array.from({length:2}, () => {
+    const hue = Math.random()*6;
+    const channel = (offset: number) => .48 + .5*Math.max(0,Math.min(1,Math.abs((hue+offset)%6-3)-1));
+    return [channel(0),channel(4),channel(2)];
+  });
+  updateColors(); render();
+});
+get('rerender').addEventListener('click',render);
+get('reset').addEventListener('click', () => {
+  colors = [[.999,.999,.999],[.999,.999,.999]];
+  get('mirror-swatch').style.background = '';
+  get('glass-swatch').style.background = '';
+  render();
+});
+quality.addEventListener('change', () => {

+});
+get('download').addEventListener('click', async () => {
+  if (downloading) return;
+  downloading = true;

+    let blob: Blob | null;
+    if (ready) blob = await new Promise<Blob|null>(resolve => canvas.toBlob(resolve,'image/png'));
+    else blob = await (await fetch(`${base}render-preview.png`)).blob();

+    link.download = `smallpt-${Date.now()}.png`; link.href = url; link.click();
+    setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url),1000);
+  } finally { downloading = false; }
+});
+const dialog = get<HTMLDialogElement>('about-dialog');
+get('about-open').addEventListener('click',()=>dialog.showModal());
+get('about-close').addEventListener('click',()=>dialog.close());

+# Rewards registration integration
+
+The form is in `index.html`, with `rewards.css` and `rewards.js`. This repository serves static files and has no registration backend. Registration fails safely and retains input until the endpoints below are deployed on the same HTTPS origin. No member is created locally, and no personal information is stored in browser storage or URLs. No account password is collected.
+
+## API contract
+
+- `GET /api/rewards/csrf`: return JSON `{ "csrfToken": "<unpredictable session-bound token>" }`. Set the session cookie with `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, and an appropriate `SameSite` policy. Return `Cache-Control: no-store`.
+- `POST /api/rewards/register`: accept JSON containing `fullName`, `email`, `favoriteDrink` (`hot`, `iced`, `tea`, or `none`), `marketingOptIn` (boolean), and `termsAccepted` (boolean). Require the session cookie and matching `X-CSRF-Token`; reject untrusted origins and unexpected content types. Return a 2xx JSON `{ "registered": true }` only after registration has been durably committed. Return `Cache-Control: no-store`.
+- Enforce `Idempotency-Key` atomically so retries cannot create duplicate memberships. Bind keys to the session and payload, and replay the original result on retries. The client retains the key for an unchanged submission, including after timeouts.
+- Independently validate all input server-side: nonempty trimmed Unicode names up to 100 characters, a valid email up to 254 characters, an allowed drink value, actual booleans, and explicit acceptance of the terms. Client validation is only a usability aid. Enforce request size limits, rate limits, and duplicate-account privacy; do not reveal whether an email already belongs to a member. Verify email ownership before granting access to membership data.
+- Keep marketing consent optional and separate from service communications. Record the terms version and consent timestamps server-side. Do not log tokens or personal information. Escape data when rendering it, and use parameterized database queries.
+- Serve the page and API over HTTPS, redirect HTTP before serving the form, and configure HSTS and appropriate CSP/security headers at the host. Form code uses external JavaScript, no HTML insertion, and no third-party submission service.
+- Publish `/rewards/terms` and `/privacy-policy` with the program's approved policies before launch; these existing-style routes are linked from the review step.
+
+The UI accepts success only from a successful JSON response with `registered: true`. HTTP failures, unexpected responses, timeouts, and missing CSRF support retain entered details and show a retry message. Without JavaScript, registration remains disabled with an explanation.

+# Rewards registration integration
+
+This repository is a static website. The registration UI is implemented, but production registration requires the following same-origin HTTPS endpoints. No registration is simulated or saved in browser storage.
+
+## Endpoint contract
+
+- `GET /api/rewards/csrf`: return `application/json` with `{ "csrfToken": "session-bound-token" }`. Use `Cache-Control: no-store`. Bind the token to a secure session cookie.
+- `POST /api/rewards/register`: accept JSON containing `givenName`, `familyName`, `email`, `password`, `birthMonth` (number or null), `birthDay` (number or null), `marketing` (boolean), and `terms` (boolean). Require a valid `X-CSRF-Token` header and verify the request origin. Return a successful status and `application/json` with `{ "success": true }` only after membership creation is confirmed.
+- All other outcomes must return an appropriate non-success status. The UI presents a generic retry message without exposing account existence or raw server error content.
+
+## Required server protections
+
+Validate all fields on the server: nonempty names of at most 80 characters, valid email up to 254 characters, password of 12–128 characters, a valid month/day pair or two nulls, and explicit terms acceptance. February 29 is supported. Do not trim or silently truncate passwords. Hash passwords using a current, vetted password hashing implementation. Record terms version and acceptance time; record marketing consent separately and never infer it from membership acceptance. Apply rate limits, email verification, and duplicate membership handling. Prevent duplicate account creation using a database uniqueness constraint and a safe retry policy.
+
+Set session cookies to Secure, HttpOnly, and an appropriate SameSite value. Enforce HTTPS; send HSTS, a suitable CSP, and anti-framing headers. Never log passwords, CSRF tokens, or raw registration payloads. Serve sensitive responses with `Cache-Control: no-store`. Permit only the intended same-origin JSON requests, without permissive CORS.
+
+The UI uses a 15-second request timeout. A connection loss can happen after a server commit, so retries must be safe and email verification/account recovery should resolve uncertain outcomes.
+
+The existing `/privacy-policy`, `/rewards-terms`, and `/account` links also need working production destinations and approved copy before launch.
+
+## Local checks
+
+`node --check rewards.js` checks JavaScript syntax. No build tool is required. Browser testing and development servers were intentionally not used.

+# The Daily Grind: field INP monitoring
+
+The homepage loads the self-hosted `assets/inp.js` module, built from
+`src/inp.js` and Google's pinned `web-vitals/attribution` dependency. It observes
+real pointer and keyboard interactions throughout the page visit, including
+back/forward cache restores. No synthetic interactions or UI changes are added.
+
+## Collector setup
+
+**This repository serves static files and does not include an analytics backend.**
+Configure your hosting layer to route `POST /analytics` to a collector that
+accepts JSON, persists it, and returns a successful response (for example, 204).
+Alternatively, change the homepage's `inp-endpoint` meta content to your existing
+collector URL. For a cross-origin collector, configure JSON POST CORS/preflight
+and permit the origin in CSP `connect-src`. An empty meta content disables
+monitoring. Until a collector is connected, requests will not retain field data.
+
+Reports contain `schemaVersion`, `page`, metric `id`, `value`, `delta`, `rating`,
+and `navigationType`. All durations are milliseconds, and interaction timestamps
+are relative to the page's performance time origin. Store the latest report per
+metric `id` (upsert), since visibility transitions can deliver multiple updates.
+Do not add successive `value`s or count updates as separate visits. Restoring a
+page from bfcache starts a new metric ID. Visits without eligible interactions,
+or without Event Timing API support, produce no INP report; do not count these
+as zero. Monitor the 75th percentile of final INP values: good <=200 ms,
+needs improvement >200–500 ms, poor >500 ms.
+
+## Diagnosing delays
+
+- `interactionTarget` uses explicit `data-inp-target` labels, such as
+  `order-online` and `seasonal-details`, with pointer/keyboard type and load state.
+- `inputDelay`, `processingDuration`, and `presentationDelay` distinguish a busy
+  main thread before the event, event processing, and the wait for the next paint.
+- `longestScript` includes script URL, function, character offset, invoker type,
+  intersecting duration and the INP subpart assigned by web-vitals. `scripts`
+  contains the five longest scripts overlapping the interaction, with
+  `scriptCount` indicating the full count. Use matching production source maps
+  to resolve minified function names and character offsets.
+- Forced style/layout timings identify synchronous work inside scripts;
+  `renderStyleDuration` and `renderLayoutDuration` sum rendering work across
+  intersecting Long Animation Frames. These frame-wide totals provide context
+  and may include work outside the interaction. They should not be added to the
+  three INP subparts. `totalScriptDuration`, `totalStyleAndLayoutDuration`,
+  `totalPaintDuration`, and `totalUnattributedDuration` are the library's
+  interaction-level estimates. The paint value estimates off-main-thread
+  presentation time; it is not a direct measurement of GPU or raster work.
+- Unsupported timings are `null`, never inferred as zero. Older implementations
+  can expose combined `forcedStyleAndLayoutDuration` and
+  `totalStyleAndLayoutDuration` without separate style/layout values. Without
+  Long Animation Frames, basic INP and its subparts remain available. LoAF only
+  captures long frames and scripts over its reporting threshold, so missing
+  script details do not imply that no JavaScript ran.
+
+No page text, input values, page query parameters, or raw DOM objects are sent.
+Script URLs omit queries/fragments; function names and URLs have length caps.
+Keep future target labels static and free of user information.
+
+## Delivery and maintenance
+
+The reporter replaces a queued `fetchLater()` snapshot whenever INP changes.
+The browser sends the latest snapshot when the page is discarded. If the API is
+unavailable or rejects a request (for example, quota restrictions), a lifecycle
+fallback sends on hidden using Beacon, then keepalive fetch if Beacon rejects.
+It also handles reports created while already hidden. There are no unload
+handlers, polling timers, persistent client queues, or console-only reporting.
+Delivery remains best effort, subject to browser policies and network failures.
+
+Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm build` after editing
+the instrumentation. Commit the generated `assets/inp.js` and license file:
+the existing static hosting command serves these directly, without a runtime CDN
+or a build server. No server is needed for the tests.
+
+References: [web-vitals attribution](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/web-vitals#attribution-build),
+[INP cause attribution](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance/guides/performance/identify-inp-causes).

+# The Daily Grind — field INP monitoring
+
+The homepage loads the committed, self-hosted `assets/inp-monitor.js` bundle. There is no runtime CDN dependency and no change to the storefront UI. Source is in `src/`; run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm build`, and `pnpm test` after editing it. No server is needed to build or test.
+
+## Connect field collection
+
+This repository contains a static site, **not a telemetry ingestion service**. Measurement and the `daily-grind:inp` event are enabled immediately. Remote collection requires a real collector:
+
+1. Provide a same-origin POST endpoint through your hosting platform or reverse proxy (for example `/telemetry/vitals`). It must accept an `application/json` body and return a successful status, typically `204`. Do not configure a static HTML path as the endpoint.
+2. Set `<meta name="inp-endpoint" content="/telemetry/vitals">` in `index.html`. Empty content disables remote transmission. Foreign origins are intentionally rejected.
+3. Store the payload and receive time. Upsert by `(page, id)`, retaining the highest `sequence` if reports arrive out of order. Keep the latest absolute `value`; do not sum values or count each update as a separate visit. BFCache restores receive new metric IDs from the library.
+
+Reports use `navigator.sendBeacon`, falling back to `fetch` with `keepalive` if the browser cannot queue the beacon. Transport is best effort; network failures are swallowed and there is no persistent retry queue. No endpoint is invented or called by default.
+
+An existing analytics integration can instead subscribe before the page becomes hidden:
+
+```js
+window.addEventListener('daily-grind:inp', ({ detail }) => {
+  // Forward detail to your analytics collector.
+});
+```
+
+## Read a report
+
+- `value` is INP in milliseconds, with the library's `rating`, `delta`, navigation type, and metric ID. All visits with a measurable INP are reported, including good ones, so a field distribution can be computed.
+- `attribution.interactionTarget` identifies the homepage control via a static `data-inp-target` label. Unlabelled elements fall back to their tag name. `interactionType`, `loadState`, and timestamps supply context.
+- `attribution.phases` separates **input delay**, **event processing**, and **presentation delay**. `dominantPhase` highlights the largest component. Presentation delay includes waiting for the next paint; it is not exclusively layout work.
+- `attribution.longestScript` identifies the longest script overlapping the interaction: source URL, function, character offset, invoker type, duration, forced style/layout time, library-assigned subpart, and overlap with each INP phase. Script duration includes forced style/layout; do not add those two fields together.
+- `attribution.longAnimationFrames` contains up to five overlapping frames, each with its eight longest scripts, blocking duration, rendering start, and style/layout start. Omission counts make truncation explicit; the library's longest culprit is preserved separately.
+- `attribution.totals` contains the library's estimated script, style/layout, paint, and unattributed durations across the interaction. These estimates are separate from the INP phase breakdown; do not sum both breakdowns. Frame and script entries may straddle the interaction window, so use script `overlap` when inspecting a phase rather than charging its entire duration to INP.
+
+Use the 75th percentile of the latest INP values across visits, segmented by device class if your collector supplies it. Good INP is at most 200 ms; needs improvement is above 200 through 500 ms; poor is above 500 ms. Investigate slow reports by target, dominant phase, and script source. Timings indicate overlapping work, not proof that every script caused the delay.
+
+## Lifecycle, support, and data minimization
+
+Google's `web-vitals/attribution` calculates INP and manages page visibility and BFCache restores. Default reporting delivers the latest changed metric on page hide, avoiding a request for every click. No interaction means no INP report; an unsupported browser also produces no INP report. Neither case is a zero score. The default event duration threshold is 40 ms; very short interactions may use the library's first-input fallback.
+
+Long Animation Frame/script details depend on browser support and attribution visibility. `capabilities` records API availability; empty frame arrays and null totals indicate unavailable evidence, not absence of work. Small scripts, inaccessible cross-origin work, and frames below the long-frame threshold may not be attributed. Paint and layout timings are estimates, not a full DevTools trace.
+
+Reports contain a fixed page label rather than the visitor's URL, no text or input values, and no DOM objects. Script URLs retain origin and pathname but omit credentials, query strings, and fragments. Keep `data-inp-target` labels static. No cookies, user identifiers, or persistent storage are added by this monitor.
+
+## Validation
+
+`pnpm test` uses Node tests for native entry serialization, attribution and phase overlap, missing LoAF support, bounded payloads, target labels, URL redaction, beacon transport, fetch fallback, and failure isolation. `pnpm build` bundles the production script. +# Daily Grind performance audit
+
+Audited November 15, 2026. Scope: the complete repository, consisting of one
+static HTML page and its start command. No browser, dev server, preview server,
+or server entrypoint was run. There is no build step. Findings are based on
+source inspection, downloaded asset bytes, image metadata, and static checks;
+they are not Lighthouse scores or measured Core Web Vitals.
+
+## Findings and changes
+
+| Area | Finding | Outcome |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| LCP discovery | Hero URL was discoverable only through inline CSS, with no explicit image priority. | Replaced the background with an HTML picture/img discoverable by the preload scanner. The single hero uses eager loading and high fetch priority. No extra preload is necessary for this early HTML image, avoiding a possible duplicate fallback download. |
+| Image transfer | Every viewport requested the same 1350px Unsplash image, adding an external connection. | Local, metadata-free WebP variants with srcset and sizes; progressive JPEG fallback. Same photo, composition, dark overlay, and centered cover behavior. |
+| CLS and resizing | The original fixed-height background already reserved hero space; no async insertions or web font swaps exist. Mobile viewport changes could resize a vh-based hero. | Retained reserved space, added intrinsic image dimensions and a minimum hero height. Small viewport units stabilize mobile toolbar resizing, with vh fallback. This is preventive work, not evidence that the original page had poor CLS. |
+| Interactions / INP | There are no scripts, handlers, hydration, timers, third-party widgets, or long JavaScript tasks in the source. | Retained native links and zero client JavaScript. No code-level JavaScript bottleneck was found; INP cannot be inferred from this alone. |
+| Mobile layout | A nonwrapping navigation and a 250px minimum grid track could overflow narrow screens. | Navigation stacks and wraps on small screens; grid tracks can shrink to container width. Mobile navigation scrolls with the document rather than occupying a large sticky overlay. |
+| Input feedback | Small navigation/footer targets and no deliberate focus styling. | At least 44px-tall navigation/footer links and visible keyboard focus. Existing color transitions respect reduced-motion preferences. |
+| CSS and fonts | Small inline stylesheet, system fonts, no stylesheet imports. | Retained inline CSS and system fonts: no additional blocking requests. Content containment would add complexity to a page with just three cards, so it was not added. |
+| Caching | Origin/CDN configuration is not present in the repository. | Image filenames include content hashes for safe future immutable caching. Actual cache headers and compression remain deployment configuration, not verified changes. |
+| Navigation destinations | Thirteen links point to routes whose implementations are absent from this repository. | Preserved destinations. Destination response times, backend operations, and logout behavior cannot be audited here. No speculative prefetching of account or logout routes. |
+
+## Measured resource sizes
+
+The baseline is the exact original URL fetched during this audit with curl:
+`https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1495474472287-4d71bcdd2085?auto=format&fit=crop&w=1350&q=80`.
+Its response was a 1350×900 JPEG of 157,968 bytes. Unsplash's automatic format
+negotiation may return a different format/size to a real browser; reductions
+below compare with that downloaded JPEG, not all possible original responses.
+
+| Resource | Bytes | Reduction vs downloaded original hero |
+| --- | ---: | ---: |
+| Original hero, 1350px JPEG | 157,968 | — |
+| WebP, 640px | 18,428 | 88.3% |
+| WebP, 960px | 32,702 | 79.3% |
+| WebP, 1350px | 53,896 | 65.9% |
+| WebP, 1920px | 93,340 | 40.9% |
+| JPEG fallback, 1350px | 113,337 | 28.3% |
+
+The browser selects one format and one candidate according to viewport width,
+pixel density, and its selection heuristics; these are alternatives, not five
+downloads. The new 1920px option supports larger/high-density displays. Mobile
+devices with high pixel density may choose a larger variant than 640px.
+
+HTML gzip size increased from 1,736 to 2,095 bytes to describe responsive images
+and mobile styles. With the 1350px WebP, HTML plus image is 55,991 bytes versus
+159,704 previously (64.9% less), excluding HTTP headers. These are transfer-size
+comparisons; no elapsed-time or CWV improvements have been measured. Runtime
+third-party resource origins fall from one to zero. Client JavaScript remains
+zero bytes.
+
+## Verification
+
+- `npm run audit:performance` passes without starting or importing a server.
+  It checks a 3 KiB gzip HTML budget, per-image transfer budgets, local asset
+  existence/content hashes, responsive candidates, JPEG fallback, explicit hero
+  sizing, eager/high priority, and absence of client JavaScript or CSS image
+  request chains. It uses only Node built-ins and does not fetch anything.
+- ImageMagick `identify` decoded every image and confirmed the expected widths
+  and preserved 3:2 composition (640px height rounds to 427px).
+- `git diff --check` passes.
+- No visual verification or runtime performance trace was performed, as requested.
+
+## Deployment and field follow-up
+
+At the actual hosting layer, serve hashed images with
+`Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. Revalidate HTML using
+`Cache-Control: no-cache` and enable Brotli/gzip for HTML. WebP and JPEG are
+already compressed. Verify actual response headers rather than assuming the
+static server supports a particular header configuration file. New image bytes
+must receive new hashes and updated HTML references.
+
+Use existing production RUM or CrUX data, if available, to compare mobile and
+desktop 75th-percentile LCP, INP, and CLS before and after release. TTFB,
+compression, cache hits, and linked-route latency require deployed responses.
+No production URL, traffic data, or hosting configuration was provided, so those
+remain unmeasured. No additional analytics or service worker was introduced.
